Grade: Grade 5
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.6: Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What do you do to ensure you do not fumble while reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

• Study the example.

▸ Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation

Teach
• Focus skill: apply fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Imitative speaking Phonetic awareness Modelling Engagement Pronunciation
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you do to ensure you do not fumble while reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
